Immortalize

ih-MOR-tuh-lyze · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To immortalize is to give enduring fame to.

The sculptor hoped to immortalize the fallen soldiers with a bronze statue that would stand in the town square for centuries.

Worked Example

The band's biggest hit immortalized their hometown, drawing tourists to the small diner mentioned in the lyrics forty years later.

Immortalize means to preserve something in lasting fame -- through a monument, a work of art, or a story -- so it is remembered long after the moment has passed.

remember vs. immortalize

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of immortalize.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — im-

prefix — im-: not (Latin)

root — mortal

root — mortal: subject to death (Latin (mortalis))

suffix — -ize

suffix — -ize: to make or cause to become (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: im- ("not") + mortal ("subject to death") + -ize ("to make") = to make (someone or something) as if untouched by death -- to grant lasting fame.

Use the root in a new word: mortality

Use the root in a new word: mortality: The same root gives us "mortality," the state of being subject to death -- the exact opposite of what immortalize creates.
